Q1: Tetrachloroethylene demonstrates a comprehensive hazard profile with Tier 1 (Known Hazards) classifications for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity and reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental hazards (ENV), inhalation hazards (IHL), oral hazards (ORL), dermal and eye hazards (SKN), and organ and systemic hazards (OGN). It also has a Tier 2 (Expanded Perspective) classification for endocrine disruption hazards (EDC), reflecting an assessment beyond GHS standards.
Q2: Tetrachloroethylene is identified on several significant lists of concern, highlighting its recognized hazards. These include California's Proposition 65, the EPA's Drinking Water Standard, the list of Hazardous Air Pollutants, and IARC Carcinogens (group 2A). It is also listed by the Endocrine Disruption Exchange (TEDX) as a potential endocrine disruptor.
Q3: Tetrachloroethylene is exceptionally well-characterized, evidenced by 26,000 scientific literature references, which is far above the typical median. Its precise molecular formula (C2Cl4) and classification as a 'Small Molecule,' along with not being a UVCB, confirm it is a well-defined substance. The absence of any Tier 4 (data deficient) ratings across its hazard profile further underscores its comprehensive assessment.
